what: DEATH RECORD — the archive had none
detail: Died 15 NOVEMBER 1924 at PRESA, Piedimonte Etneo, aged SEVENTY-NINE, a CONTADINO; certificate number 15. Aged 79 in November 1924 gives a birth in 1845, at Piedimonte Etneo -- which matches the ages the marriage proclamations gave him in 1898, 1902 and 1910 and CORRECTS the family tree, which says 1850. His father is named as MARIANO and his mother as MARIA CATALANO; his wife as LEONARDA BONANNO.
source: Italy, Catania, Catania, Civil Registration (Tribunale), 1866-1929 — FamilySearch 1:1:XWTK-5R8Q

what: THE NAME LINE CONFIRMED FROM A RECORD
detail: The archive reached Mariano Mazza and Maria Catalano by inference from marriage proclamations that call Rosario 'di Mariano'. Rosario's own death act names BOTH parents outright -- Mariano and Maria Catalano -- which converts the deepest Sicilian generation from an inference into a documented fact.
source: Italy, Catania, Catania, Civil Registration (Tribunale), 1866-1929 — FamilySearch 1:1:XWTK-5R8Q

what: A SON THE ARCHIVE DID NOT HAVE
detail: The Acireale diocesan registers carry a parish record naming ROSARIO MAZZA and LEONARDA BONANNO as the parents of a MARIANUM MAZZA -- a son named for his paternal grandfather, exactly as Sicilian custom predicts for a first son. The family tree does not have him.
source: Italy, Catania, Diocesi di Acireale, Catholic Church Records, 1560-1950

detail: The parish register of Piedimonte Etneo records the marriage in LATIN: Salvator Mazza, son of ROGERIUS MAZZA and LEONARDA BONANNO, to MARIA NICOTRAM, daughter of JOANNES NICOTRAM and VENERA COSENTINO. Rosario appears as 'Rogerius', which is why a search for 'Rosario' in these registers returns nothing.
source: Piedimonte Etneo parish register, Marriage Records 1777-1911 — FamilySearch 3:1:3QS7-99ZG-7XNZ

what: A THREE-WAY CONFLICT, NOT A TWO-WAY ONE
detail: The archive already held two readings of Maria Nicotra's mother: 'Monti Venera' from the 1898 civil proclamation and 'Venera Cassaneti' from the Queensland death index. The parish register of the same 1898 marriage gives a THIRD: VENERA COSENTINO. The given name Venera is constant across all three; the surname is read three different ways. Cassaneti and Cosentino may be the same word badly read. Unresolved.
source: Piedimonte Etneo parish register; 1898 civil proclamation; Queensland BDM

what: THEIR MARRIAGE — FOUND. PIEDIMONTE ETNEO, 30 APRIL 1871, ATTO 14
detail: The act the archive has wanted for a fortnight. On 30 APRIL 1871, at four in the afternoon in the casa comunale of Piedimonte Etneo, before Barone Mariano, sindaco, ROSARIO MAZZA and LEONARDA BONANNO were married. Both are called CELIBI -- neither had been married before -- both BORN AND RESIDENT there, and both BRACCIANTI: she worked the land alongside him. He is entered as twenty-six, she as twenty-six. HIS PARENTS ARE NAMED: figlio di MARIANO e di MARIA CATALANO. HERS ARE NAMED FOR THE FIRST TIME ANYWHERE: figlia di GAETANO e d'ANNA CAVALLARO. Witnesses: Salvatore Greco, 38, calzolaio, and Antonino Di Lava fu Giuseppe, 46, bracciante. Act 15 follows at half past four the same afternoon, so the register was doing a run of weddings that day. The parish register was the wrong door: the film's own index held no marriage for the pair. Civil registration began in 1866, so an 1871 marriage is a CIVIL act, and the civil act is the one that names all four parents.
source: Piedimonte Etneo, Matrimoni 1871, atto 14 — Antenati ark an_ua83392, images 13-14

who: Rosario Mazza's children in the parish registers
what: FOUR MORE, UNDER FOUR SPELLINGS OF HIS NAME
detail: The Acireale diocesan registers carry several children of Rosario Mazza and Leonarda Bonanno, and the father's name is transcribed differently almost every time: ROGERIUS Mazza with a son Salvator; ROSARIUS Mazza with a son HORATIUS (Orazio); JOANNES Mazza with LEONORA Bonanno and a son Joannem (Giovanni); GASPARE Mazza with Leonarda Bonanno and a son SANTO. The last is the more interesting: SANTO MAZZA is one of the two sons this archive found missing from the family tree, and here is a parish record of him. The lesson for searching these registers is that the given name is unreliable and the WIFE'S name is the stable handle.
source: Italy, Catania, Diocesi di Acireale, Catholic Church Records, 1560-1950

what: HIS BIRTH ACT — BORN 2 JUNE 1845, ATTO 64
detail: Found by working backwards from the marriage. ATTO DI NASCITA no. 64 of 1845, Comune di Piedimonte, distretto di Acireale, Provincia di Catania: MARIANO MAZZA, DI ANNI TRENTASEI, di professione BRACCIALE, appeared before the sindaco Antonino Grassi and presented a boy born to MARIA CATALANO, of thirty-six, and to the said Mariano Mazza, on the SECOND DAY OF JUNE 1845 at eleven in the morning, NELLA CASA DI LORO ABITAZIONE, and gave him the name ROSARIO. The baptism column has the parish of the Chiesa Maggiore returning the notice the same day, 2 June 1845, for ROSARIO MAZZA. This is the whole of the deepest Sicilian generation in one page: it CONFIRMS the death act's Mariano and Maria Catalano from an independent register, it FIXES Rosario's birth to a day, and it dates MARIANO MAZZA HIMSELF to about 1809 and MARIA CATALANO to about 1809.
source: Piedimonte Etneo, Nati 1845, atto 64 — Antenati ark an_ua72387, image 66

what: A WHOLE GENERATION THE TREE DOES NOT HAVE
detail: Leonarda Bonanno has stood in this archive as a name with a father's first name attached -- 'daughter of Gaetano', from the 1910 marriage proclamation. The marriage act of 1871 gives her BOTH parents outright: GAETANO BONANNO and ANNA CAVALLARO of Piedimonte Etneo. They are the Bonanno equal of Mariano Mazza and Maria Catalano, and like them they are ENTIRELY ABSENT FROM THE FAMILY TREE.

what: THE WHOLE SERIES IS NOW LISTED, AND ITS INDEX IS BETTER THAN AN INDEX
detail: Fifty volumes of Piedimonte births, 1820 to 1863, with their Antenati arks, are now written down in data/pe-arks.tsv. Two things make this series unusually cheap to work. First, each volume ends with a REGISTER OF THE WHOLE YEAR -- not an alphabetical tavola but a ruled table, six openings long, listing every birth IN ACT ORDER with the child, the comune, BOTH PARENTS and the day. A year of births can be read in six page-loads. Second, the index is a finding aid for PARENTS, not just children: to find every child of Mariano Mazza and Maria Catalano it is enough to read the parents column down each year. That is the next sweep, and it will give Rosario's brothers and sisters.
source: Antenati, Stato civile della restaurazione, Piedimonte (oggi Piedimonte Etneo), serie 72189

what: THE ACT READ — PIEDIMONTE ETNEO, MATRIMONI 1836, ATTO 17. STILL A LEAD, AND ONE WORD OF IT WAS MINE, NOT THE REGISTER'S
detail: The act itself, found at image 35 of the volume: in these registers the filled ATTO DELLA SOLENNE PROMESSA sits on the right-hand page of every ODD image, so act = (image - 1) / 2. 7 SEPTEMBER 1836, twenty-three o'clock Italian time, before Raffaele Gulli, second eletto acting as sindaco. MARIANO MAZZA, of anni TRENTA, born at Piedimonte, of profession BRACCIALE, domiciled in this comune, son of IGNAZIO and of GIUSEPPA PULVIRENTI, aged SIXTY. And AGATA CATALANO, of anni VENTOTTO, BORN AT MACCHIA, domiciled in this territory, daughter of the LATE CARLO and of MARIA CARDILE, aged SIXTY. Married in church the next day, 8 September 1836. FIRST, A CORRECTION OF THIS ARCHIVE'S OWN. The index column was read here as 'Mazza ORAZIO'. The act says IGNAZIO. The act wins, and the argument built on the other reading -- that Rosario named a son Orazio, so Orazio was a family name -- IS WITHDRAWN. It was an argument from a misreading. WHAT THE ACT SETTLES AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. For: he is the only Mazza Mariano groom in sixteen years of this register; he is a BRACCIALE, exactly as in 1845; he is Piedimonte-born, as in 1845; the surname Catalano is right; and the BRIDE'S AGE FITS -- 28 in September 1836 is a birth about 1808, and Rosario's mother is 36 in June 1845, a birth about 1809. Against: the bride is AGATA here and MARIA in both of Rosario's acts; and the GROOM'S AGE IS THREE YEARS OUT -- 30 in 1836 gives 1806, where 1845 gives 1809. So: PROBABLE, NOT PROVEN. Ignazio Mazza and Giuseppa Pulvirenti are not drawn on any chart and are not in the documented additions.
source: Piedimonte Etneo, Matrimoni 1836, atto 17 — Antenati ark an_ua72256, image 35 (act), image 52 (index)

what: HOW FEW THEY WERE — THE NEGATIVE SWEEPS
detail: Worth writing down because it changes what to expect. The birth registers of 1844 and 1846 were read ENTIRE -- 128 births in one year, 146 in the other -- and contain NO MAZZA AT ALL. 1845 contains two: Rosario, act 64, and an Alfio Mazza, act 90, son of INNOCENZO MAZZA and DOMENICA CAVALLARO. Across sixteen years of marriages, 1830-1845, the Mazza appear four times: Mariano as a groom in 1836, and three Mazza women as brides -- Domenica in 1842 (to Pietro Sorbello), Alfia in 1844 (to Mariano Sorbello) and one more. So the Mazza were a SMALL family at Piedimonte in the 1830s and 1840s, not a numerous one. Rosario may have had few brothers and sisters, or none surviving; and the 111 unjoined Mazza in the family tree are very unlikely to be Piedimonte cousins.
source: Piedimonte Etneo, Nati 1844 and 1846 read complete; Matrimoni 1830-1845 indexes read

detail: The Matrimoni, processetti of Piedimonte Etneo would hold the spouses' own birth certificates, filed with the marriage -- the cleanest possible test of whether the Mariano Mazza of 1836 is Rosario's father. The series exists and was listed in full: TWENTY volumes, and they run 1841 to 1860. THERE IS NO 1836. That route is closed, and the question has to be settled some other way -- most likely by Mariano's own birth act, if Ignazio Mazza and Giuseppa Pulvirenti can be found in the birth registers from 1820, or by his death act.

what: HER BIRTH ACT — BORN 7 NOVEMBER 1843, ATTO 101
detail: Found the same way as her husband's: by reading the annual table of the whole year. Entry 101 of the Piedimonte births of 1843 reads BONANNO LEONARDA -- Piedimonte -- BONANNO GAETANO / CAVALLARO ANNA. The act itself: on 8 November 1843, before the sindaco Antonino Grassi, GAETANO BONANNO, DI ANNI TRENTASEI, di professione BRACCIALE, domiciled there, presented a girl born to ANNA CAVALLARO, DI ANNI TRENTOTTO, and to the said Gaetano Bonanno, on the SEVENTH day of November at eight in the morning, NELLA CASA DI LORO ABITAZIONE, and gave her the name LEONARDA. Baptised the same day at the Chiesa Maggiore. So GAETANO BONANNO was born about 1807 and ANNA CAVALLARO about 1805, and both are now dated as well as named. And Leonarda was TWENTY-SEVEN when she married on 30 April 1871, not twenty-six as her marriage act says -- one more declared age a year out.
source: Piedimonte Etneo, Nati 1843, atto 101 — Antenati ark an_ua72385, image 103

who: Gaetano Bonanno and Anna Cavallaro's marriage
what: NOT AT PIEDIMONTE, 1828-1845 — EIGHTEEN YEARS READ
detail: The marriage indexes of Piedimonte Etneo were read for EIGHTEEN CONSECUTIVE YEARS, 1828 to 1845, and there is NO GAETANO BONANNO among the grooms. Three Bonanno appear in those years, all of them women marrying out. Gaetano was born about 1807, so a marriage before 1828 would have him under twenty-one; possible, but the likelier reading is that they married in ANNA CAVALLARO'S OWN COMUNE and only then settled at Piedimonte -- which is what the Mazza marriage of 1836 shows happening the other way about, with a bride from Macchia. The Piedimonte volumes 1820-1827 are listed and unread; after that the search moves to Macchia, Mascali and Giarre.
source: Piedimonte Etneo, Matrimoni 1828-1845, annual indexes — Antenati serie 72189

what: FOUR YEARS READ ENTIRE, AND HE HAS NONE IN THEM
detail: The Piedimonte birth registers of 1844, 1845, 1846 and 1847 have now been read in full -- something over five hundred births. MAZZA MARIANO and MARIA CATALANO appear in ONE of them: Rosario, act 64 of 1845. No brother, no sister, in the two years before him or the two years after. The only other Mazza births in those four years belong to a DIFFERENT couple: MAZZA INNOCENZIO and CAVALLARO DOMENICA, who have an Alfio at act 90 of 1845 and a Sebastiana at act 31 of 1847.
source: Piedimonte Etneo, Nati 1844, 1845, 1846, 1847 — annual tables read complete

what: AN OPEN QUESTION THAT WOULD JOIN TWO THREADS OF THIS ARCHIVE
detail: This archive already holds a second Piedimonte Mazza line, reached from the other end: the marriage acts of 1874 and 1876 make ANTONINO MAZZA and SALVATORE MAZZA both 'figlio d'INNOCENZIO e di DOMENICA CAVALLARO'. The birth registers now put the same couple in the 1840s, with an Alfio in 1845 and a Sebastiana in 1847 -- in the same comune, in the same years, as Rosario. AND THE 1836 MARRIAGE ACT MAKES MARIANO MAZZA THE SON OF AN IGNAZIO. Ignazio and Innocenzio are not the same name, but a man called Ignazio with a son called Innocenzio is entirely ordinary, and if Innocenzio and Mariano were BROTHERS then the archive's other Piedimonte Mazza are ROSARIO'S FIRST COUSINS and two threads join. NOT A FINDING. The test is Innocenzio's own marriage act, which would name his father. It is not in the Piedimonte indexes 1825-1845 -- the only Mazza groom in twenty-one years is Mariano in 1836 -- so Innocenzio married before 1825 or in another comune, exactly as the Bonanno appear to have done.
source: Piedimonte Etneo, Nati 1845 atto 90, Nati 1847 atto 31; Matrimoni 1874 atto 26, 1876 atto 5
